events.title: Hormuz tanker war; Brent ~$106, commercial transits still a fraction of normal
events.why_it_matters: Ship-tracking shows only ~9 commodity transits on the latest day versus a pre-war ~125 large vessels/day, keeping a war premium in G3 inflation and the Warsh extra-hike path.
events.what_to_watch: Any phased-reopen leak, AIS 'dark' tanker counts, and whether Brent holds above $100 into PCE/NFP week.

events.title: China Mid-Autumn / Golden Week travel surge begins
events.why_it_matters: Overlapping Mid-Autumn and National Day holidays should lift domestic services/travel prints, but EV/rail substitution has already killed the old Golden Week gasoline spike.
events.what_to_watch: Rail/air passenger peaks around Oct 1, tourism spend vs 2025's record, and whether gasoline demand stays flat-to-down YoY.

events.title: Trump–Xi White House summit; trade truce extended to Jan 10
events.why_it_matters: Bessent's two-month extension removes the Nov 10 tariff-cliff tail and buys negotiation runway, but no broader deal on rare earths, AI, or Taiwan was announced.
events.what_to_watch: Whether working-level talks produce a longer arrangement before Jan 10, and any post-summit export-control or rare-earth friction.

events.title: US–Iran UNGA shuttle talks on reopening Hormuz
events.why_it_matters: First real contact in months was called 'very productive,' but Iran denies dropping preconditions (end blockade, lift pressure, unfreeze assets), so oil remains headline-driven.
events.what_to_watch: Follow-up mediated rounds and whether Tehran's 'reopen within seven days if conditions met' offer gets a US counter.

events.title: 80 countries demand urgent Hormuz reopening at UNGA
events.why_it_matters: A GCC-plus-West joint statement condemns Iranian/Houthi interference and demands unimpeded transit with no tolls, raising diplomatic pressure without reopening the strait.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the statement is a prelude to a naval/coalition escort plan or just UN theater.

events.title: Trump–Zelenskyy UNGA push for Ukraine energy/Black Sea truce
events.why_it_matters: A limited energy-infrastructure or grain-corridor pause would ease the diesel crunch from Russian refinery hits, but the Kremlin still rejects a simple ceasefire and has not moved on territory.
events.what_to_watch: Whether US-mediated talks actually reconvene in October and if strikes on energy assets pause.

events.title: Graham Russia/Iran Act signed; up to 100% secondary tariffs
events.why_it_matters: Law now requires up-to-100% tariffs on top buyers of Russian crude/gas that keep buying, a live escalation channel into China/India trade and crude flows, with presidential waiver discretion.
events.what_to_watch: USTR country list and whether the 30-day 'new purchases' clock after enactment is used against China or India.

events.title: FY2027 CR already law through Dec 11; Sept 30 shutdown risk dead
events.why_it_matters: H.R. 6500 / P.L. 119-103 was signed Sept 2, so the Oct 1 funding cliff the prior scan flagged is not live; next fight is the Dec 11 lame-duck CR.
events.what_to_watch: Nothing this window; drop unless House hard-liners try to reopen the CR.

events.title: US Section 338 import bans on selected Canadian goods take effect
events.why_it_matters: Sept 8 proclamations convert parts of the 50% Canada tit-for-tat into outright bans on specified beer/wine/spirits, some whey, and >800cc motorcycles at 12:01 a.m. ET Sept 29.
events.what_to_watch: Canadian retaliation list and any last-minute product carve-outs or in-transit entries still paying 50%.

events.title: IEEPA tariff refunds; CAPE Phase 3 and Federal Circuit appeal
events.why_it_matters: Post-SCOTUS IEEPA invalidation, CBP is refunding unliquidated entries while DOJ appeals CIT's universal finally-liquidated refund order; Phase 3 is targeted around Oct 6.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Phase 3 actually opens and if the Federal Circuit stays refunds for non-litigants.

events.title: Google ad-tech remedy: behavioral only, AdX not divested
events.why_it_matters: Unsealed Brinkema opinion (ruling Sept 2) spares AdX, orders interoperability/non-discrimination for six years — a relief for GOOGL and a negative for ad-tech plaintiffs.
events.what_to_watch: DOJ/Google appeal path; implementation clock (~60 days from final judgment).

events.title: August PCE, personal income, and Q2 GDP third estimate + NIPA revisions
events.why_it_matters: First post-Warsh-hike inflation print; consensus clusters around core PCE +0.24–0.28% m/m and ~3.3–3.4% y/y, with annual NIPA revisions that could shave y/y and reprice the extra 2026 hike.
events.what_to_watch: Core PCE m/m vs 0.28%, revision to y/y, and whether Q2 GDP stays near the 1.5% second estimate.

events.title: September nonfarm payrolls (October 2 jobs report)
events.why_it_matters: August was +162k; consensus now +90–110k and U-3 4.1–4.2%. A hot print cements ~65–72% Oct 28 hike odds; a miss revives the Warsh-overtightening debate.
events.what_to_watch: Headline NFP vs 100k, unemployment vs 4.2%, AHE, and revisions to August.

events.title: August JOLTS job openings
events.why_it_matters: Opens labor week into NFP; consensus ~7.2m after July's ~7.27m, a gauge of how much tightness the Warsh Fed still sees.
events.what_to_watch: Openings vs 7.2m and the quits rate; a sub-7.0m print would lean against an October hike.

events.title: Conference Board consumer confidence (September)
events.why_it_matters: Oil-at-$106 and the Warsh hike are the two things that can crack spending intentions before PCE.
events.what_to_watch: Index vs ~89 and the expectations/jobs-plentiful differential.

events.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (September)
events.why_it_matters: August printed 54.6; one preview is 55.5. A still-expanding factory sector plus oil shock is the hawkish mix for Warsh.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs 55, prices-paid, and new orders.

events.title: August new-home sales beat at 684k SAAR
events.why_it_matters: Sales jumped 6.4% m/m to 684k (vs ~615–620k expected), showing the housing crack in existing sales/starts has not fully hit new-home demand after the Warsh hike.
events.what_to_watch: Whether mortgage-rate backup after oil/JGB spillover reverses the beat in the next print (Oct 27).

events.title: BoJ 1.25% policy rate; 10y JGB at three-decade highs
events.why_it_matters: Highest BoJ rate in 31 years (Sept 18, 7-2) is transmitting into JGBs (~3.07% 10y on Sept 24) and global duration just as G3 tightening is otherwise unfinished.
events.what_to_watch: 10y JGB holding above 3%, yen, and whether Oct 29–30 BoJ (just outside this window) signals another hike.

events.title: Takaichi fiscal stimulus / Japan debt-jitter debate
events.why_it_matters: Growth package, food-tax cut talk, and record FY2027 budget requests are colliding with BoJ hikes, feeding the JGB selloff and global duration spillover.
events.what_to_watch: Size/financing of the next stimulus bill and any MOF/BoJ jawbone on super-long JGBs.

events.title: Japan Tankan large manufacturers (Q3)
events.why_it_matters: QUICK/CME consensus is +25 current DI (from +22), a read on whether rate hikes and energy costs are biting capex before the late-October BoJ.
events.what_to_watch: Large-mfg DI vs +25, outlook DI, and capex plans.

events.title: PBOC pledges appropriately loose policy; LPR held 16th month
events.why_it_matters: Accommodative pledge plus a stable yuan into the Xi visit is incremental easing, not a bazooka; 1y/5y LPR stay 3.0%/3.5% and near-term cuts look unlikely.
events.what_to_watch: Golden Week liquidity ops and whether September PMI (Sept 30) forces a RRR/LPR move.

events.title: China NBS PMI (September) into Golden Week
events.why_it_matters: Official mfg PMI was 49.8 in August (fourth sub-50 stretch); another contraction into the holiday would keep the 'exports strong, consumption dead' split in play.
events.what_to_watch: Mfg PMI vs 50, non-mfg vs 49.0, and high-tech vs broad split.

events.title: China August activity: IP +5.2% vs retail +0.4%
events.why_it_matters: Factory/high-tech resilience versus stalled consumption is why Beijing is doing targeted trade-in/bank capital measures rather than a 2024-style bazooka.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Golden Week services data breaks the 0.4% retail trend.

events.title: Eurozone HICP flash (September)
events.why_it_matters: August final was 3.2% y/y after a 3.3% flash, driven by energy +14.3%; another hot print keeps a non-trivial chance of an ECB hike at the Oct 29 meeting (just outside this window).
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs 3.2% and energy contribution; German flash CPI on Sept 30 is the sneak preview.

events.title: UK Q2 GDP third/quarterly release
events.why_it_matters: BoE held 3.75% on Sept 17 (6-3, three hikers); a firm GDP print into energy inflation keeps sterling rates sticky with no October MPC.
events.what_to_watch: QoQ vs ~0.4% and whether the three hawks get more data cover for November.

events.title: OPEC+ eight-country meeting on November quotas
events.why_it_matters: The Sept 6 virtual meeting froze October targets after completing the last 188 kb/d unwind; Oct 4 decides November against a Hormuz-disrupted physical market.
events.what_to_watch: Hold vs another pause, and any 2027 baseline/quota language.

events.title: Micron FY Q4 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Only mega-cap-adjacent AI/memory bellwether reporting this week; guide on HBM/DRAM tightness is the sector tape into a Mag7-quiet window.
events.what_to_watch: FY27 HBM supply commentary, gross margin, and any China/export-control language.

events.title: Nike FY Q1 2027 and Accenture FY26 earnings
events.why_it_matters: NKE is the China/consumer-demand tell; ACN is the IT-services/AI-spend tell. No Magnificent-7 reports until late October.
events.what_to_watch: Nike Greater China and full-price mix; Accenture bookings and generative-AI commentary.

events.title: Oura IPO pricing window (~$2.1–2.2bn)
events.why_it_matters: Largest consumer/healthtech deal in this window (50m shares at $40–44, mostly secondary) is a risk-appetite test with Mag7 earnings still a month away.
events.what_to_watch: Whether it prices at/above $44 and first-day pop vs a secondary-heavy overhang.

events.title: SpaceX staggered lockup tranche (~7% eligible)
events.why_it_matters: Another ~328m Class A shares become eligible; prior tranches saw ~4% one-day dips. Musk remains locked into 2027.
events.what_to_watch: Actual Form 144 supply vs eligibility, and whether the Oct 24 tranche is already being pre-positioned.

events.title: Anthropic IPO marketing window (confidential S-1)
events.why_it_matters: Sources have pointed to a mid-October launch after a June confidential S-1; a $1T-scale AI listing would dominate risk appetite even if pricing slips past this window.
events.what_to_watch: S-1 public filing / roadshow launch this week or next; slippage into post-midterms would be the tell.

events.title: Samsung/SK Hynix vs KEPCO grid-prepay fight
events.why_it_matters: Memory majors rejected a ~$18.6bn electricity prepay to fund chip-cluster power; this is the binding constraint on AI HBM expansion, not the summer heat wave (no Sept fab-outage reports).
events.what_to_watch: Any KEPCO/government compromise and Yongin/southwest cluster power timelines.

top_risks: Hormuz stays effectively closed and UNGA talks fail, holding Brent >$100 and forcing Warsh/ECB extra hikes.
Hot Aug PCE (Sept 30) and/or Sept NFP (Oct 2) push October 28 hike odds from ~2/3 toward fully priced.
JGB 10y >3% plus UST backup spills into global duration, housing, and high-multiple tech.
Graham Act secondary-tariff implementation hits China/India energy buyers and reopens a US–CN trade shock after the Jan 10 truce.
US–Canada Section 338 bans on Sept 29 trigger a wider goods-retaliation loop into autos/ag/consumer.
top_opportunities: A credible Hormuz reopen path (even phased) would collapse the oil/inflation premium and ease the extra-hike narrative.
US–China truce to Jan 10 is a six-week risk-on runway for trade-sensitive cyclicals and semis if working-level talks stay quiet.
Soft JOLTS/NFP would reopen the 'Warsh over-tightening' debate and bid duration/housing.
Micron guide as a clean AI-memory tape with Mag7 silent until late October.
Ukraine energy-infrastructure truce would help European diesel and industrial margins even without a full ceasefire.
summary: The Sept 24 Trump–Xi pageant extended the trade truce to Jan 10 and removed the Nov 10 cliff, but it did not de-risk the market: Hormuz is still barely open (Brent ~$106, single-digit daily transits), UNGA diplomacy produced no deal, and futures have lifted October 28 hike odds to roughly two-thirds. This window's live catalysts are Canada Section 338 bans (Sept 29), labor/PCE week (Sept 29–Oct 2), China PMI into Golden Week (Sept 30), Micron (Sept 30), and the Oct 4 OPEC+ meeting — not a US shutdown, which is already funded through Dec 11.
